title: Diagnose the layer
scenario: App A, connected to your files, answers questions about your project and remembers decisions. App B — reportedly running the same underlying model — refuses to see any files and forgets between sessions.

options.text: The two apps run completely different models; sharing models is not possible.
options.feedback: Models are routinely shared: one engine can power many apps and platforms. The difference lives above the engine.

options.text: Products layer features — file access, memory, tools — around models; App B simply does not expose them.
options.feedback: Exactly. Same engine, different product features. Check what a product enables before blaming the model.

options.text: App A's model was specially retrained on your files.
options.feedback: No retraining happened — your files are read into the context when needed, not learned into the model's weights.

options.text: File access is a property of the model itself, so App B must use a weaker version.
options.feedback: File access is a product feature. A “weaker version” is not the explanation unless the documentation says so.

hints: Which layer owns memory, files and tools?
explanation: Model, product, feature: the engine sets the ceiling; the product decides what is reachable. Most “same model, different behaviour” puzzles are product-layer differences — tools, memory, defaults and policies.
